objective.scope: Fixed 10-minute sequence, 519 deterministic fixture matches, 13 courts, 3200–6400 ms points, full parsed BTP integration every 30 seconds. Not a direct live-server A/B proof.

user_live_reference.note: Partial web export with all 1188 receipts; different real tournament, TLS and workload. Not an exact A/B baseline for the deterministic HTTP fixture.

reception.clock: Worker Date.now at WebSocket message callback; monotonic hrtime also forwarded

limitations: Isolated deterministic 519-game fixture, real durable NeDB and unmodified committed BTS modules.
Real separate testclient simulates tablets, TV and admin; point interval in options, 13 courts, zero score gap.
Idle fixture games explicitly set to scheduled before measurement, enabling automatic calls after real finishes.
Periodic sync uses the actual validated integration planner but updates idle match numbers directly in staging; no periodic BTP TCP/XML fetch/parser.
Full BTP fixture is used only at bootstrap. No live tournament or server is modified. Officials/tabletoperator allocation disabled.
Automatic preparation enabled; 26 pairs of players recur across scheduled games, creating real participant dependencies. No winner/loser bracket propagation simulated.
One explicit unchanged court call during first integration; automatic calls through actual score finishes; free announcements every two seconds.
Queue samples every 20 ms, diagnostics/traces enabled by normal client. Observer overhead and local machine load included.
Reception of WebSocket events, no browser painting or audible speech. Limited duration, no capacity guarantee.

comparison_rules: Only compare identical workload, duration, point intervals, sync intervals and reception method.
The preparation-btp workload exercises the complete parsed BTP integration; it does not use BTP TCP/XML or real winner/loser brackets.
Server and receiver are real separate processes; actual NeDB persistence and score/admin/display handlers are used.
No test suites or CPU profiling ran alongside measured benchmarks.
The live server at localhost:4433 was unreachable; no live data was altered.

limits: The live server was unreachable; no live-tournament capacity or TLS/real-bracket guarantee is inferred.

The representative fixture starts checked in; the measured scenario generated no check-in writes. Check-in races and rules were covered by targeted and full-suite tests, and occurred in the separate higher-load long run.
Full parsed BTP integration is exercised; real TCP/XML, doubles, official allocation and winner/loser bracket progression are outside this fixture.

The 4x faster continuous point stress workloads exceed the target and are retained, including the recent 90-second bounded-write result of 41/41 ms. The achieved target is scoped to the original point cadence and test phases.
The two endpoints are actual WebSocket reception in an isolated receiver thread, not browser painting or audible playback.

The last representative run lost no archived diagnostic samples or receipts. The earlier 6283-update stress run explicitly dropped 1283 individual receipt records while keeping its complete cumulative latency statistics.
